rationale: Free open-weight models runnable on the owner's CPU-only laptop (i7-1355U, 15.7 GB RAM, no CUDA). Straight quantisations of official Qwen weights; fine-tuned, distilled or abliterated variants are excluded. The benchmark decides between candidates.

runtimeVulkan.note: The same llama.cpp release built for Vulkan, so the laptop's integrated graphics can share the work. Not pinned here: resolved on the machine from GitHub's published sha256 digest for this exact asset (local-model.mjs resolve runtime-vulkan), and used only if model-tune.mjs measures it faster than the CPU build.

upgradeNote: The decision model for the debate and TradingAgents: the largest candidate the machine's RAM fits that its repository actually has (tried in this order), pinned on the machine to Hugging Face's published LFS sha256 at an exact commit, and used only after it passes our exams (model-upgrade.mjs). Names that do not exist are skipped. The 4B keeps the bulk work.

server.note: Loopback only; the API key is passed through the environment, never the command line. Thinking is off (any stray reasoning is separated into reasoning_content) so replies stay strict JSON and CPU time is not spent on hidden reasoning.
